operators.notes: Scan supplier, filter by regex pattern on varlen s_comment. Produces tiny set of bad suppkeys.
Tiny hash set of excluded supplier keys for NOT IN anti-join.
All three filters applied during scan. p_brand and p_type use dictionary codes for fast comparison. p_size uses 8-element bitset or flat array lookup.
Build hash map on filtered part rows. Payload stores dictionary-coded brand/type (uint16) and size (int32) for compact layout. ~300K entries fits in L3 cache (44MB).
Fused operator: scan partsupp → probe part hash map (inner join) → check anti-join hash set → feed to aggregation. Single pass over partsupp.

Two-phase COUNT(DISTINCT): Phase 1 — per-thread hash_set<(group_key, ps_suppkey)> for dedup during parallel scan. Phase 2 — merge thread-local sets, then count per group. Group key encoded as composite of dictionary-coded brand (uint16) + type (uint16) + size (int32) = 8 bytes.
Sort ~18K result rows. Small enough for single-threaded pdqsort. Decode dictionary strings for final string comparison on brand/type.
Decode dictionary codes to strings for output. Can be deferred to sort step or done here.

join_order.notes: Tiny anti-join set checked inline during partsupp scan
Filtered part fits in L3 cache. Probe during single partsupp scan.

data_structures.part_hash_map: compact_hash_map<int32, struct{uint16 brand_code, uint16 type_code, int32 size}>(pre_sized=524288)
data_structures.p_size_filter: bitset<50> with bits set at positions {3,9,14,19,23,36,45,49}

parallelism.notes: Supplier scan is tiny (100K rows), single-threaded. Part scan (2M) and partsupp scan (8M) parallelized. Aggregation merge of ~18K groups is fast single-threaded.

notes: Standalone tail — no shared components consumed. Pipeline: (1) build tiny anti-join set from supplier, (2) build part hash map with dictionary-coded payloads (~300K entries, fits L3), (3) parallel scan partsupp fusing probe + anti-join + dedup aggregation in single pass, (4) merge per-thread dedup sets and count groups, (5) sort ~18K result rows. Critical optimization: p_size IN filter uses 50-bit bitset; brand/type filters operate on dictionary codes avoiding string comparison.
